answers.text: Three lines every time for the driver's message, same order — drop-off time, pallet count, damage noted. Time in 24-hour format, pallet count as a plain number, and if nothing's said about damage, write 'none noted' instead of leaving it blank. If the driver leaves one of the three out altogether, write 'not given' rather than guess. That keeps the log tidy.

Follow-up list needs the same four columns every time, same order — time, customer, topic, outcome — with a count of how many need follow-up at the top. Only count entries marked 'call back' or 'no answer', not the ones marked 'resolved'.

This note doesn't hold together as written, so I wouldn't file it yet. It's not the crew size or the six hours — the problem is the finishing day: access is from 8am on the 22nd, and six hours from 8am finishes early afternoon that same day, not 'early afternoon on the 23rd' like it says. That's a full day off. I'd want to look at that again before it's filed.
9 out of 118 paid late does work out to about 92%, so that part's fine. But 96 to 118 is closer to a 23% rise, not the 20% stated, so that number's off.
I'd sign off Output 2 — it shows 940 and 827, not just the 88%. Output 1 only gives the percentage, no ticket counts to check it against.

I'd send Email 2 as is — it's got the actual volume numbers in it, 1,200 up to 1,650. Email 1 just says 'we'd expect a better rate' without saying by how much our volume's grown, so there's nothing to check that against.

1. Vendor's line-item pricing — no, that's the vendor's confidential detail. 2. Procurement spend, aggregate — yes, fine. 3. Unsigned budget draft — no, not released yet. 4. Vendor datasheet — yes, already public. 5. Employee's home address — no, that's personal.
Hourly rates and the retainer cap I'd hold back — commercial detail, not for a tool we haven't checked. The NDA clause needs the same care, since it names the client directly.
I'd have the monthly totals cross-checked against the warehouse system directly, not just eyeballed. That happens before the summary goes to finance at month-end, not after.

Step 1 worries me the most — if the AI misreads the invoice PDF, the wrong numbers carry through the whole rest of the process. I'd want someone keeping an eye on the process generally, just to be safe.
